text:
ashwin: Heads up — canary pool in eu-central1 started evicting gpus during the BMC fancurve push around midnight. ~8% of nodes moved to degraded due to thermal trip events. Noticed bmc reboot loops on 3 hosts.

maria: ack. Which firmware image did the canary run? was this the v1.4.2-fancurve tweak we queued yesterday?

ashwin: yes, v1.4.2 with fan-profile: reduced idle RPMs to save power. Canary runbook used group `canary-fan-lower` — logs show `watchdog: thermal_override` then `secure_boot: toggled -> 0` on two nodes. odd.

leo: that secure boot toggle is alarming. we have a safety check that prevents boot changes, unless BMC resets to factory. could the reboot wipe a register?

ashwin: ipmi console shows BMC uptime restart -> nvram fallback after watchdog. I put snippets in the artifact bucket: gs://infra-artifacts/bmc/canary/3267890123/logs.txt

infra-tools: deploy-bot: Canary deployment `canary-fan-lower` completed at 2026-03-20T00:13Z on 12 hosts (eu-central1). Metrics: ambient temp +1.2C, avg fan rpm -22%.

sre-jen: rolling this back now. I'm triggering manual rollback to previous fan profile and forcing BMC cold-reset runbook on the 3 affected hosts. Runbook steps I ran:```bash
# rollback fan profile
infractl bmc set-fan-profile --hosts host-241,host-256,host-263 --profile default
# soft power-cycle BMC
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $HOST -U admin -P **** mc reset cold
```

maria: thanks. can you also pin those hosts out of autoscaler and drain GPU pods? we already saw job evictions affecting realtime inference in eu-c. cost spike from retries was visible in last billing window.

leo: pinging platform-scheduler to avoid rescheduling heavy GPU jobs onto the canary hosts. @kai can you check if provisioning backlog in eu-c will cause us to shift capacity from us-west?

kai: seeing 14% headroom used in eu-central1. If we keep draining ~40 GPUs it'll push some queued infra-provision jobs to us-west which adds ~0.8ms p99 network latency for model shards and ~12% egress cost. estimate monthly delta ~+$4.3k if sustained.

ashwin: noted. priority is safety + restore canary. Cost follow-up with finance after rollback.

sre-jen: rollback finished for the 3 hosts. BMCs came back, secure_boot flags read as `1`. I flushed NV-RAM and updated watchdog tuning to be less aggressive in micro-reboots. Observability: GPU evictions dropped to baseline in 7m.

maria: good. can we mark this fancurve change as a fail and add a preflight check to our rollout? e.g., verify BMC watchdog delta < 5s and nvram persistence test on a sample host.

leo: agree. I'll add a preflight test to the rollout pipeline. Proposal: extend canary window to 24h for any BMC/fan/thermal firmware changes + automated nvram-read after reboot.

infra-tools: deploy-bot: Created issue #infra/4372-thermal-fan-preflight with steps and assigned to leo + ashwin.

kai: also propose adding cost-signal alert: if node evictions cause cross-region failover above 10% within 30m, fire `cost-provision` page so finance/GTM can triage quick.

maria: yes — link the alert to an automated scaling policy rollback if cost delta > $1k/hr and capacity can be satisfied in-region.

ashwin: final notes: this was probably an interaction between lower idle RPM + BMC watchdog threshold. Not malware — nvram fallback path needs testing. Thanks all for fast rollback. I'll do a root-cause doc and schedule a postmortem if we see recurrence. :white_check_mark:

leo: thanks — please paste the RCA draft in #postmortems when ready.

oncall-bot: Incident closed: `canary-fan-lower` — rollback successful. Duration: 00:18:57.

ashwin: uploading shortlisted logs + ipmitool dumps to the ticket now.

maria: follow-up action items: 1) preflight tests 2) deploy pipeline change 3) cost alert rule 4) update runbook with explicit ipmitool nvram-check. assigning owners in the issue.

sre-jen: adding a small thermal margin to default profile (+10% idle rpm) until we validate new fan curves on 48hr canary.

ashwin: 👍
